column1: # Module 03 — CS50P accelerated. Format: Text<TAB>Extra<TAB>tags (Extra optional). Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
In Python, what is a variable? {{c1::A name stuck on a value}} — reassigning {{c1::moves the label, not the contents}}.
column2: A labelled jar.

column1: What are Python's three starter types and their literals? Text {{c1::str "text"}} · whole number {{c1::int 42}} · decimal {{c1::float 12.5}}.
In Python, what does "2" + "2" evaluate to? {{c1::"22"}} — + on strings {{c1::glues text}}.
column2: Convert with int() first if you meant maths.

column1: In Python, what is the difference between return and print? return {{c1::hands a value to the caller}}; print {{c1::only shows pixels to a human}}.
column2: Returned values are usable and testable; printed ones are gone.

column1: What is a parameter vs an argument? Parameter = {{c1::the placeholder name in the def}}; argument = {{c1::the actual value passed in the call}}.
In Python, what type does input() always return? {{c1::str — even if the user typed a number}}.
column2: Convert before arithmetic.

column1: In Python, what is = vs ==? = {{c1::assigns}}; == {{c1::compares}}.
column2: Sticks the label vs asks a True/False question.

column1: Which branch of a Python if/elif chain runs? {{c1::The FIRST true one only — the rest are skipped}}.
column2: So the narrowest/highest test goes first.

column1: In Python, what owns an indented block? {{c1::The if/for/while/def line above it}}.
column2: Indentation IS the syntax; four spaces.

column1: In Python, when do you use for vs while? for = {{c1::for each thing in a collection}}; while = {{c1::keep going until this stops being true}}.
What are the four steps of the accumulator pattern? {{c1::Start the accumulator}} · {{c1::visit each item}} · {{c1::fold it in}} · {{c1::return the result}}.
What is the first index of a Python list, and what does items[len(items)] raise? {{c1::0}} · {{c1::IndexError}}.
column2: len(items) counts; the last valid index is len(items)-1.

column1: How do you read a Python traceback? {{c1::Bottom-up — the last line is what went wrong}}.
column2: The lines above are where it happened.

column1: Why never write a bare except: in Python? {{c1::It swallows EVERY alarm}} — catch {{c1::the specific exception}}.
column2: Including the typo you needed to hear.

column1: What is the Python retry-until-valid input idiom? {{c1::while True + try/break on success + except ValueError: ask again}}.
In Python, what is sys.argv[0]? {{c1::The script's own name}} — your first real argument is {{c1::sys.argv[1]}}.
What is the fastest Python laboratory you own? {{c1::The REPL}}.
column2: Run python alone, experiment one line at a time, exit().

column1: What three things make a unit test GOOD? {{c1::It fails when behaviour breaks}} · {{c1::it tests boundaries}} · {{c1::its name says what it guards}}.
column2: Boundaries: 0, empty, negative.

column1: Why can't you assert on print in a test? {{c1::print returns None}} — structure logic in functions that {{c1::RETURN}}.
column2: Then assert on the returned value.

column1: What is the safe file-reading idiom in Python? {{c1::with open(path) as f:}}
column2: Closes the file for you, even when errors happen.

column1: In Python's open(), what do modes "w" and "a" do? "w" {{c1::REPLACES the file's contents}}; "a" {{c1::appends}}.
column2: Know which you meant BEFORE you run it.

column1: What is the phantom \n bug when reading files? Lines keep their newline — {{c1::.strip() before comparing}}.
column2: Or .rstrip("\n") to keep leading spaces.

column1: What is the count-dict idiom using a plain dict and .get (no imports)? {{c1::counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1}}
In regex, what matches: a digit {{c1::\d}} · a word-char {{c1::\w}} · one-or-more {{c1::+}} · optional {{c1::?}} · one-of-these {{c1::[abc]}} · a capture group {{c1::()}}
Why use raw strings for Python regex? {{c1::r"..." stops Python eating backslashes before the regex engine sees them}}.
What regex matches every dd/mm/yyyy date? {{c1::r"\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}"}}
column2: Use with re.findall to pull all dates from text.

column1: In OOP, what is a class vs an object? Class = {{c1::the cookie cutter (blueprint)}}; object = {{c1::the cookie (instance)}}.
column2: hi.upper() is a method on a str object.

column1: In Python, what is self? {{c1::The object being operated on}} — passed to methods {{c1::automatically}}.
In Python, what does @property do? Makes a method {{c1::readable like an attribute — no parentheses}}.
column2: e.g. w.volume instead of w.volume().

column1: In Python, what does __str__ control? {{c1::What print(obj) and str(obj) show}}.
column2: The human face of your object.

column1: Write a Python list comprehension for the squares of the even numbers in nums: {{c1::[x*x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]}}
column2: A loop that builds a list in one line.

column1: In Python, sort a dict's items by value descending, ties alphabetical: {{c1::sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))}}
column2: Negate the value for descending; the tuple breaks ties.

column1: De-duplicate a Python list in one call: {{c1::set(items)}} — order not guaranteed; deduped AND sorted: {{c1::sorted(set(items))}}.
column2: Keep ORIGINAL order instead: list(dict.fromkeys(items)).
